issues.description: Field name inconsistency in Person entity: the template Person.java declares the field 'firstName' (private String firstName) while the solution Person.java declares a field named 'forename' but its getters/setters and equals()/hashCode() still reference 'firstName'. Tests and other code (e.g., PersonServiceTest) call setFirstName/getFirstName. This mismatch in identifier names in the solution will cause compilation failures and prevents students from running or testing the project.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person model identifier consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the field 'forename' in solution/src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java back to 'firstName' and ensure all getters, setters, equals(), and hashCode() use the same 'firstName' identifier. Alternatively, if keeping 'forename', update all getters/setters, equals(), hashCode(), repository and test usages to refer to 'forename' (less recommended). Ensure tests and template remain aligned with the chosen identifier.

issues.description: The Person entity's first-name attribute is named inconsistently across artifacts. In the template Person class (template_repository/src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java) the field is declared as 'private String firstName' and the code/tests call getFirstName()/setFirstName(). In the solution Person class (solution_repository/src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java) the field is declared as 'private String forename' while the rest of the code and tests still use getFirstName()/setFirstName(), producing a mismatch between the field name and the accessor names and between template/tests and the solution implementation. This inconsistency prevents a clear mapping from the problem/tests to the implementation and will likely cause compilation errors or confusion for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier for the person's first name across all artifacts. The least disruptive fix is to rename the field in solution_repository/src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java from 'forename' to 'firstName' and ensure the getters/setters reference that same field (getFirstName()/setFirstName()). Alternatively, if preferring 'forename', rename all usages in template, tests, and REST/service code to use 'forename' consistently — but prefer restoring 'firstName' to match the template, tests, and the problem context.
